Calque of Byzantine Greek Ἀνάργυρος (Anárguros), from Ancient Greek ἀνάργυρος (anárguros, “without money”), from ἀν- (an-, “un-”) + ἄργυρος (árguros, “silver, money”). By surface analysis, бес- (bes-, “without”) + (poetic) сребро́ (srebró, “silver”) + -ник (-nik).

parole.significato: leap (referring to leap years, leap days, etc.)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic високостныи (visokostnyi), from високостъ (visokostŭ, “leap day”), from Byzantine Greek βίσεξτος (bísextos), from Late Latin bissextus, from Latin bisextus.

From Byzantine Greek κάτεργον (kátergon, “galley; penal labor”), from Ancient Greek κάτεργος (kátergos).

parole.significato: cell (room in a monastery for sleeping one person)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic келиꙗ (kelija), from Byzantine Greek κελλία (kellía), plural of κελλίον (kellíon, “garret”), diminutive of κέλλα (kélla), from Latin cella.
Borrowed from Medieval Byzantine Greek κρεβάτιον (krebátion), from Ancient Greek κράββατος (krábbatos). See also Modern Greek κρεβάτι (kreváti), Serbo-Croatian krevet.

parole.significato: rusalka; a Slavic female water spirit associated with death by drowning and with Green Week traditions occurring around…
parole.testo: Inherited from Old East Slavic русалиꙗ (rusalija), Old Church Slavonic роусалиѩ (rusaliję) + -ка (-ka), from Byzantine Greek ῥουσάλια (rhousália), from Latin rōsālia (“festival of the roses”). Compare with Bulgarian руса́лия (rusálija).
Borrowed from Byzantine Greek ῥάσον (rháson), from Latin rāsus (p.p.p. of rādō). Compare typologically дерю́га (derjúga) (akin to драть (dratʹ)).

parole.significato: garfish, needlefish (a fish from the Belonidae family; most commonly, Belone belone)

parole.significato: enamelling (decorative application of vitreous enamel to metal; especially in reference to traditional Russian art)

Borrowed from Byzantine Greek φανάριον (phanárion, “lamp, torch”). Suffix influenced by -а́рь (-árʹ). Compare Modern Greek φανάρι (fanári).
